text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp said Tuesday that it had encountered another prolific fault block in the northeastern quadrant of the Bob West North natural gas field, in south Texas.

Citing the successful drilling results of its new Esperanza No. 1 well in Zapata County, TransTexas said that it believes the ultimately recoverable reserves from the field were likely to further increase as a result of the increased aerial extent.
The Esperanza No. 1 was drilled to a depth of 9,000 feet and encountered 91 feet of net pay in the L1, L2 and L3 sands of the Upper Wilcox formation in an interval between 7,600 and 8,250 feet.
The well is northeast ot the most recently drilled well, the Palmyra No. 7, which is producing at 52.4 million cubic feet of natural gas per day.
